title: Relative flatness of a finitely presented space module eventually descends
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces and their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use quasi-coherent modules [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and canonical tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme, and quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. An affine morphism is representable and has affine source after pullback to any affine scheme test. A morphism is of finite presentation if it is quasi-compact, quasi-separated, and locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts; local finite presentation means chart ring maps have finitely many generators and relations. A module is finitely presented if etale locally it has an exact presentation $\mathcal O^m\to\mathcal O^n\to M\to0$ with $m,n$ finite. Flat over a base means that every geometric stalk of the module is flat over the corresponding geometric local ring of the base. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, $(T_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of affine schemes with affine transitions and limit $T$, and $i_0\in I$. Let $f_{i_0}:X_{i_0}\to T_{i_0}$ be a finitely presented algebraic space. For $i\ge i_0$ put $X_i=X_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T_i$, $f_i:X_i\to T_i$, and put $X=X_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T$, $f:X\to T$. Let $M_{i_0}$ be a quasi-coherent finitely presented module on $X_{i_0}$, and write $M_i$ and $M$ for its ordinary tensor pullbacks to $X_i$ and $X$. If $M$ is flat over $T$, there is $j\ge i_0$ such that $M_k$ is flat over $T_k$ for every $k\ge j$.

source.place: Tag 08K0 (lemma-descend-flat), module assertion in Situation 084W (situation-descent-property), specialized to affine bases and finite-presentation source; persistence under base change is spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 05VW (lemma-base-change-module-flat).

proof.text: Since $f_{i_0}$ is quasi-compact and $T_{i_0}$ is affine, the scheme test $T_{i_0}\to T_{i_0}$ in the definition makes $X_{i_0}$ quasi-compact. Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $p_0:U_0\to X_{i_0}$ with $U_0$ affine by [lem-trf-space-qc-finite-affine-atlas-refinement]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] with target chart the identity of $T_{i_0}$: the scheme morphism $g_0=f_{i_0}p_0:U_0\to T_{i_0}$ is locally of finite presentation. Write $R_i=\Gamma(T_i,\mathcal O_{T_i})$ and $B_0=\Gamma(U_0,\mathcal O_{U_0})$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] to the whole affine source and target proves that $B_0$ is a finitely presented $R_{i_0}$-algebra.

source.place: Tag 08K0 (lemma-descend-flat), first paragraph choosing affine charts and final paragraph checking local finite presentation; target chart is the given affine base.

proof.text: The atlas pullback $p_0^*M_{i_0}$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent]. For the etale map $p_0$, tensor pullback is restriction to the slice site with the restricted structure ring by [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization]. Thus the given local finite free presentations restrict to local finite free presentations of $p_0^*M_{i_0}$. Let $F_0$ be its corresponding quasi-coherent Zariski module, using [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. Finite presentation is preserved and reflected by this comparison by [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison], so $F_0$ is finitely presented. Therefore $N_0=\Gamma(U_0,F_0)$ is a finitely presented $B_0$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine].

source.place: Tag 08K0 (lemma-descend-flat), restriction of the finitely presented module to the affine source chart; scheme comparison and Properties Tag 01PC (lemma-finite-presentation-module).

proof.text: For $i\ge i_0$ put $U_i=U_0\times_{T_{i_0}}T_i$ and put $U=U_0\times_{T_{i_0}}T$. The fibre-product universal property also identifies these with $U_0\times_{X_{i_0}}X_i$ and $U_0\times_{X_{i_0}}X$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] the maps $p_i:U_i\to X_i$ and $p:U\to X$ are surjective etale atlases. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], $T\simeq\operatorname{Spec}R$ for $R=\varinjlim_iR_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $U_i\simeq\operatorname{Spec}(R_i\otimes_{R_{i_0}}B_0)$ and $U\simeq\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_{R_{i_0}}B_0)$. The two composites to $X_{i_0}$ agree in each Cartesian square. The composition comparisons of [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization] and the scheme pullback comparison of [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] therefore identify the Zariski modules $F_i$ corresponding to $p_i^*M_i$, and $F$ corresponding to $p^*M$, with the ordinary scheme pullbacks of $F_0$. Their section modules are $N_i=R_i\otimes_{R_{i_0}}N_0$ and $N=R\otimes_{R_{i_0}}N_0$: apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] to the whole affine schemes and the balancing isomorphism $N_0\otimes_{B_0}(R_i\otimes_{R_{i_0}}B_0)\simeq R_i\otimes_{R_{i_0}}N_0$, $n\otimes(a\otimes b)\mapsto a\otimes bn$, with inverse $a\otimes n\mapsto n\otimes(a\otimes1)$; likewise with $R$ in place of $R_i$.

source.place: Tag 08K0 (lemma-descend-flat), base-change diagrams and their affine limits; scheme tensor pullback calculation underlying Tag 05LY (lemma-descend-module-flat-finite-presentation).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-module-flat-chart-test] to $X\to T$, $M$ and the atlas $p$. The hypothesis on geometric stalks says exactly that $F$ is flat over the scheme $T$. By [lem-pc-affine-chart-relative-flat-criterion], with affine open the whole $U$, its section module $N$ is flat over $R$. Apply [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-descent] to the directed ring system $(R_i)$, with initial index $i_0$, coefficient algebra $A_{i_0}=R_{i_0}$, second algebra $B_{i_0}=B_0$, and module $N_0$. The first algebra is finitely presented over itself (zero generators and relations), and the other two finiteness hypotheses were checked in steps 1 and 2. Step 3 supplies the required tensor descriptions and the ring colimit; $R\otimes_{R_{i_0}}R_{i_0}\simeq R$ by $a\otimes r\mapsto ar$. Thus there is $j\ge i_0$ such that for every $k\ge j$ the module $N_k$ is flat over $R_k\otimes_{R_{i_0}}R_{i_0}\simeq R_k$. No stage ring has been assumed Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 08K0 (lemma-descend-flat), final affine reduction; limits.tex Tag 05LY (lemma-descend-module-flat-finite-presentation), final paragraph; algebra.tex Tag 02JO (lemma-flat-finite-presentation-limit-flat), part (3).

proof.text: Fix any $k\ge j$. By [lem-pc-affine-chart-relative-flat-criterion], applied to the whole affine source $U_k$ and target $T_k$, the flat $R_k$-module of sections $N_k$ from steps 3 and 4 makes $F_k$ flat over $T_k$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-module-flat-chart-test] to $X_k\to T_k$, $M_k$, and the surjective etale atlas $p_k$ from step 3. It follows that every geometric stalk of $M_k$ is flat over the corresponding geometric local ring of $T_k$, as required. The same index $j$ works for every such $k$. If the atlas is empty, its source is $\operatorname{Spec}0$ and its section module is zero; all cited affine and chart criteria allow this case and their pointwise conditions are vacuous.

source.place: Tag 08K0 (lemma-descend-flat), passage back from affine charts to spaces; eventual persistence follows here directly from algebra.tex Tag 02JO (3), not from an extra support hypothesis.
